title: The '+' button on a palette node card does not add the node; only double-click does
reasoning: Reproduced twice on the rebuilt bundle at profile v2-sequencer-run and it does NOT reproduce. (a) Unfiltered palette: node count '1 node' -> single click on the '+' glyph of the Dither card -> '2 nodes / 1 step' with a Dither node in the sequence tree. (b) The finding's exact repro: typed 'Dither' into the palette search, single-clicked the '+' on the filtered Dither card -> '3 nodes / 2 steps'. No double-click was used in either case. The code agrees and has for two releases: node_palette.dart:800-812 wires the always-visible plus icon to GestureDetector(onTap: _addNode) with the comment 'Always-visible add button: a single tap adds the node ... Previously the only click-to-add affordance was a hidden double-tap'; git shows no uncommitted change to that file, so this is not a fix that landed after the finding. Most likely the original observation missed the icon -- the plus is only ~13px (Responsive.iconSize(context, 13) at line 689), and a click a few pixels off lands on the card, which merely selects it. That is exactly the reported symptom.

title: Pre-flight warns that a step is scheduled 'before target rises' when it is scheduled AFTER the rise time it prints
reasoning: Reproduced verbatim on the rebuilt bundle. Site 30N/82E, target 'New Target' at RA 00h00m00s / Dec +00d00'36", pressed Start at 16:54 local. Pre-Flight > Simulation printed: 'New Target: "Cool Camera" scheduled at 16:54 before target rises at 11:36', plus the same for Dither (17:04) and Unpark Mount (17:05). All three times are AFTER the 11:36 it prints. I computed the true window independently from the app's own LST readout (LST 23:12 at 16:54 local): for RA 0h/Dec 0 rise is at LST 18h -> ~11:42 local and set at LST 6h -> ~23:42 local, so the target really is above the horizon at 16:54 and no conflict exists at all. Screenshot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/32.png shows the three warnings.
location_wrong: The finding's unit points at screen:sequencer/preflight_validation_dialog.dart, but the dialog only renders strings. The text and the comparison are produced by SequenceTimeEstimator.findTimingConflicts in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart:786-798 ('before target rises at' literal at line 791); _formatTime (line 411) prints HH:mm only, which is why a rise on a different calendar day reads as one that already passed. Fix belongs in sequence_time_estimator.dart, not the dialog.

title: Pre-flight dark-library check uses the camera default temperature (-10C), not the temperature the sequence's Cool Camera node will actually reach (15C)
reasoning: Reproduced. The sequence's Cool Camera node was set to Target Temperature 15 (node chip reads '15C', Properties field reads 15). Pre-Flight > Dark Library still reported: 'No matching darks found for 1 exposure combination: gain=100, offset=50, temp=-10.0C, duration=3s, binning=1x1'. -10.0C is the camera default, not the 15C setpoint the run will hold. Screenshot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/32.png (dialog) plus tree output of the Cool Camera node chip '15C'.
location_wrong: The finding's unit says screen:sequencer/preflight_validation_dialog.dart; the dialog only renders the issue. The temperature is chosen in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/preflight_rules.dart:116-118 -- 'final cameraState = ref.read(cameraStateProvider); final camTargetTemp = cameraState.targetTemp;' -- i.e. the LIVE camera setpoint (still the -10C default before the run's Cool Camera node executes), which is then stamped onto every DarkFrameRequirement at line 139. The comment there even says ExposureNode doesn't model temperature; nothing consults the sequence's CoolCameraNode. Fix belongs in preflight_rules.dart.

title: Builder and Pre-Flight disagree about how long the same sequence takes: '~18m 54s' vs 'Duration 27m'
reasoning: Reproduced with a different sequence, so the exact numbers differ but the disagreement is real and visible in one frame. Sequence: Target > Cool Camera 15C, Dither, Unpark, Slew, Autofocus, Take Exposures 4x3s. Builder header estimate chip: '~14m 9s'. Pre-Flight > Simulation on the same sequence in the same screenshot: 'Duration 12m' and 'Ends 17:07' with a start of 16:54 -- i.e. THREE different numbers (14m09s, 12m, and 13m implied by Ends-minus-now). Evidence /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/32.png. Severity is right at P2: the magnitude I measured is ~18% rather than the 43% claimed, but the defect (two independently computed estimates on one screen) is exactly as described. I did not re-test the sub-claim that the builder chip ignores the Cool Camera setpoint; note the Cool Camera properties panel shows 'Max cooling time 10m / Duration: 10m', i.e. the builder bills the node's Max Duration, which would make that sub-claim plausible.
location_wrong: The finding's unit says screen:sequencer/preflight_validation_dialog.dart, which is only one of the two disagreeing sides. The two numbers come from two different engines: the Builder chip/timeline uses SequenceTimeEstimator (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_time_estimator.dart, called from screens/sequencer/widgets/node_timing_section.dart:119-128 and sequence_timeline.dart:55-65), while the Pre-Flight Simulation panel uses PreSessionSimulator().simulate(...) (preflight_validation_dialog.dart:134, rendered at :735). Any fix has to reconcile the two estimators, not edit the dialog.

title: A single failing Dither node is reported as two identical errors, in the report and in two stacked critical banners
reasoning: Reproduced. Sequence contained exactly ONE Dither node and no guider was connected. The native log records the failure exactly ONCE ('ERROR Dither failed: Dither failed: No active guider configured' at 20:58:06, followed by a single "Child 'Dither' completed with status: Failure"). But sequence_runs id=1 stats_json has errorMessages of length 2 with the identical string twice, and the Session Report's Errors section prints the line twice (screenshot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/35.png). So one failure occurrence -> two recorded errors, exactly as claimed. I did not catch the two stacked critical banners (they had already cleared by the time I looked), so that half of the claim is unverified; the report/DB half is confirmed on its own.
location_wrong: The finding's unit is screen:sequencer/run_dashboard/critical_event_banner.dart, but the duplication is upstream of the banner: the run's error list itself already holds two copies (stats_json), so the banner is only rendering what it was given. The double-record happens on the path into SequenceRunStats.recordError (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence_stats_provider.dart:162 has no de-dup, unlike recordWarning at :166 which does). Point a fixer at the executor's error-recording path, not at critical_event_banner.dart.

title: Session report says 'Autofocus 0' after an autofocus that ran 9 points and completed successfully
reasoning: Reproduced. Run 2 executed the Autofocus node: app.log shows 'Autofocus point 1..9 sample 1/1 completed' and "Child 'Autofocus' completed with status: Success" at 21:01:46Z, and the focuser moved 25000 -> 25070 (status bar). The Session Report's Mount / operations block reads 'Autofocus runs 0' (screenshot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/39.png), sequence_runs id=2 stats_json has autofocusRuns:0, and focus_models has 0 rows. Root cause is mechanical and total: SequenceRunStats.recordAutofocus() (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence_stats_provider.dart:160) has ZERO call sites in non-test code -- grep for 'recordAutofocus()' returns only the definition -- so autofocusRuns can never be anything but 0. By contrast recordTriggerFire and recordMeridianFlip are wired up in event_operations.dart:317 and :926.

title: Frames captured under a named target are reported as 'Untargeted', and the run's target breakdown is keyed by the SEQUENCE name instead of the target name
reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Sequence 'New Sequence' had one Target node named 'New Target'; all 4 lights ran underneath it. Session Report > Targets shows a single group 'Untargeted  4/4 frames | 1m 20s' (screenshot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/39.png). sequence_runs id=2 stats_json targetBreakdown is {"New Sequence": {"Unknown": {captured:4,...}}} -- keyed by the SEQUENCE name, with filter 'Unknown' even though captured_images.filter is 'R'. captured_images.target_id is empty for all 4 rows and the targets table has 0 rows. The keying is the documented fallback in event_operations.dart:877-883: target = progress.currentTarget ?? currentSequenceProvider.name ?? 'Sequence', i.e. currentTarget was never populated (no TargetStarted/TargetChanged consumed) so it fell through to the sequence name; filter falls back to 'Unknown' the same way.

title: The top-bar run chip still reads 'Sequence Running' (green) while the sequence is paused
reasoning: Reproduced. Run 3 paused at 17:06:37 mid-exposure. At 17:06:41 the accessibility tree simultaneously carried 'PAUSED' (node badge), 'panel: Sequence Running', 'panel: Paused', 'Paused 25%' (toolbar chip) and a 'Resume' button. The cropped capture of the Sequencer tab row (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/40.png) shows the chip rendered with a GREEN dot and the literal text 'Sequence Running' at that moment. Two indicators one row apart disagree, exactly as claimed.

title: sequence_runs.status stays 'running' while the run is paused, so any non-GUI consumer thinks the rig is still exposing
reasoning: Reproduced and additionally proven from the schema. Run 3 was paused at 17:06:37; sqlite3 on /tmp/ns-audit/v2-sequencer-run/data/skotiq.db returned status='running' for id=3 at 17:06:41 and again at 17:06:59, while the GUI showed PAUSED / 'Paused 50%' / Resume throughout. The table cannot express the state at all: .schema sequence_runs is (id, sequence_id, sequence_name, started_at, ended_at, status TEXT DEFAULT 'running', stats_json, sequence_snapshot_json) -- there is no paused_at column, and 'paused' is never written. Anything reading the DB (headless API, web dashboard, mobile) sees a running rig.
corrected_severity: P2 -- same single defect as the P2 'top-bar chip still reads Sequence Running' finding (no paused state is modelled anywhere), and this half is the one that reaches unattended remote operators, who have no GUI to correct them.

title: The Continue Session handoff dialog says 'Unknown Profile' and 'No Sequence' while naming the sequence in its own header and with a real profile active
reasoning: Reproduced on relaunch. The dialog is titled 'Continue Session', its card header prints 'New Sequence', and directly beneath it the rows read 'Equipment Profile: Unknown Profile' and 'Sequence: No Sequence' (screenshot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/42.png). The scratch DB has exactly one equipment profile, 'My Equipment' (equipment_profiles id=1), which the status bar shows as the active profile. The fallback strings the finding cites are at quick_start_dialog.dart:184-185 verbatim ('final profileDisplay = quickStartContext.profileName ?? 'Unknown Profile';' / ''No Sequence''), so the cited file:line is correct. I also found the upstream cause: the run's own imaging_sessions rows are written with profile_id NULL and sequence_id NULL (sqlite: 'select id,profile_id,sequence_id from imaging_sessions' -> 1||, 2||, 3||), and QuickStartService builds the context from imaging_sessions (quick_start_service.dart:624 lastSessionDate: session.endTime ?? session.startTime). Fixing the display string alone would not help; the session rows never record which profile or sequence ran.
location_wrong: The finding's unit field says screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart. The dialog that actually shows this is packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart (the body of the finding names it correctly); session_handoff_dialog.dart exists but is a different surface.

title: Continue Session dialog dates yesterday's session as 'Today at 14:57'
reasoning: Reproduced deliberately. I backdated the audit profile's imaging_sessions rows by 19 hours (end_time of the last session -> 2026-08-02 22:03:07 local, i.e. YESTERDAY) and relaunched at 2026-08-03 17:10. The dialog header printed 'Continue Session / Today at 22:03' while the dashboard card one layer behind it correctly said 'Paused-stopped - 19 hours ago' and the app's briefing header said 'Mon Aug 3'. Screenshot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2/42.png shows all three at once. The bug is exact and unconditional in quick_start_dialog.dart:103-116: _formatDate compares ELAPSED time, 'final diff = now.difference(dt); if (diff.inDays == 0) return 'Today at ...'', so any session less than 24h old is labelled Today no matter which calendar day it fell on -- and 'Yesterday' can only ever appear for sessions 24-48h old.
location_wrong: The finding's unit field says screen:sequencer/session_handoff_dialog.dart; the code is packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/quick_start_dialog.dart:103-116. Also the finding's repro attributes the timestamp to sequence_runs.ended_at -- it is not: I edited sequence_runs by 19h and the header did not move at all. The date comes from imaging_sessions.end_time via QuickStartService (quick_start_service.dart:624). A fixer told to look at sequence_runs would chase the wrong table.
